headline: Highest risk is medium: MinerU can feed document content into plano’s broad-egress gateway, creating leakage and cascading-error paths; prompt-injection and compliance risks are lower but non-zero.

A_prompt_injection.rationale: MinerU ingests PDFs/DOCX/XLSX and exposes an MCP server; plano is an OpenAI-compatible gateway with broad network egress. If MinerU output is bridged into plano through MCP or files, document text can be treated as instructions. The interaction is plausible in default integrations, though not directly documented, so uncertainty is escalated from low.
conditions: IF MinerU output is forwarded into plano prompts or tools without provenance tagging, prompt injection is possible.
IF the shared MCP path exposes raw document text to plano, instruction hijacking becomes feasible.
mitigations: Disable automatic forwarding from MinerU to plano.
Add provenance tags and strip instructions from extracted text before routing.
Require human review for any prompt built from document content.
Use separate MCP endpoints per agent.
requires-engineering: add content-sanitization and allowlist filters in the orchestrator.

B_data_leakage.rationale: MinerU touches PDFs, DOCX, PPTX, XLSX, OCR text, and other document data; plano has broad egress and handles logs/metrics/traces. A shared workspace or routed payloads could leak sensitive document contents into plano’s outbound requests or telemetry. No direct evidence proves the bridge, but the pairwise pathway is credible enough to rate medium.
conditions: IF extracted document text is sent through plano’s chat-completions endpoint, leakage occurs.
IF MinerU outputs are logged or mirrored into plano telemetry, sensitive content can persist outside the source system.
mitigations: Keep MinerU and plano on separate workspaces.
Disable verbose request/response logging in plano.
Redact document text before any gateway call.
Restrict plano egress destinations to approved APIs.
requires-engineering: implement DLP scanning on routed payloads.

C_capability_conflict.rationale: MinerU is read-oriented and cannot write the filesystem or modify git state; plano exposes only an OpenAI-compatible endpoint and config file. Their write surfaces do not overlap, so direct resource contention is limited. The only plausible conflict is shared configuration or routing state, which is unusual and small in blast radius.
conditions: IF both agents are pointed at the same mutable config file, last-write wins may occur.
IF an orchestrator shares a single routing state across both agents, configuration races are possible.
mitigations: Place each agent in its own config directory.
Avoid shared mutable files for routing or credentials.
Run one writer per config path.
Document ownership of any shared state.
requires-engineering: add file-locking around shared configuration writes.

D_cascading_error.rationale: MinerU produces extracted text, tables, and OCR output that plano can consume through its chat-completions gateway. If plano treats that output as authoritative, extraction mistakes can cascade into downstream decisions or responses. Because no verification step is documented between them, the interaction is plausible and medium severity.
conditions: IF plano uses MinerU output as final truth without validation, extraction errors propagate.
IF downstream workflows act on plano responses derived from unverified MinerU text, mistakes cascade.
mitigations: Insert a verification step before plano consumes MinerU output.
Require source-document citations for any extracted claim.
Flag low-confidence OCR spans for review.
Limit plano to summarization, not action-taking.
requires-engineering: add structured validation against the source document.

E_compliance.rationale: MinerU is documented as private and fully offline, while plano has broad network egress and logs/metrics/traces. This creates a compliance mismatch risk if regulated document data processed by MinerU is forwarded into plano’s networked environment. The other agent is cited because the mismatch arises from their combined handling model.
conditions: IF regulated documents processed by MinerU are routed into plano’s cloud-connected path, residency or retention obligations may be violated.
IF plano retains logs containing document-derived content longer than policy allows, compliance gaps emerge.
mitigations: Keep regulated data out of plano.
Disable or minimize retention on plano logs.
Use a data-processing agreement for any routed personal data.
Separate EU and US workloads.
requires-engineering: enforce residency-aware routing and retention controls.
